chunks: "Bus capacitance is the total capacitance between a bus line, SDA or SCL, and ground.
It's the sum of everything hanging on the wire: each device's pin and its ESD protection, the PCB trace, connectors, any cable, test points, and so on.
It matters because the pull-up resistor has to charge it every time the line goes high. The rising edge is an RC charge, so the rise time is about 0. 85 times R p times C b .
The more capacitance, the slower the edge. The I2C spec caps it at 400 picofarads for Standard and Fast mode.
Fast-mode Plus allows a bit more, but only because its drivers sink 20 milliamps, so you can use a much stronger pull-up.
A typical budget is about 5 to 10 picofarads per device pin, roughly 1 picofarads per centimetre of trace on a normal board, and tens of pF per metre of cable.
So a short on-board bus with six devices might be 80 to 100 picofarads, and a bus with a long cable can blow through 400 picofarads fast.
To check, I'd estimate from the datasheets, then measure the actual rise time on a scope and back-calculate C b equals t r over (0. 8473R p) ."
